summary: AtomKokkos::map_set_device() reallocates sametag BEFORE the map_init(0) call that may free it, so for MAP_HASH the kernel writes into a destroyed, zero-extent k_sametag view.
failure_scenario: Run with the Kokkos device atom map (default, kokkos atom/map not legacy) and atom_modify map hash (or >1e6 atom IDs so hash is auto-selected).  When this rank's nlocal+nghost grows past map_nhash (load imbalance, ghost growth), map_init(0) recreates the hash, which calls map_delete() and destroys k_sametag / sets max_same=0.  The following parallel_for then writes d_sametag(i) for i in [0,nall) into a zero-extent view: out-of-bounds device write / memory corruption (Kokkos bounds-check abort in a debug build), and k_sametag.sync_host() at line 267 leaves sametag == nullptr for all later host users (Domain::closest_image, Special).
suggested_fix: Move the 'if (nall > max_same) {...}' sametag (re)allocation block below the 'if (map_style == MAP_HASH) { if (nall > map_nhash) map_init(0); }' block, matching src/atom_map.cpp:196-201 and AtomKokkos::map_set_host().

summary: With the device atom map and MAP_ARRAY, the global->local map array is never cleared: exchange_device() skips map_clear() and map_set_device() only clears the hash, so map() returns stale local indices for atom IDs that have migrated off this rank instead of -1.
failure_scenario: GPU run with the defaults (ngpus>0 => atom_map_legacy=0, exchange_comm_legacy=0) and an atom-ID range small enough that map_style is MAP_ARRAY.  An atom whose ID once lived on this rank migrates away; a bonded partner lookup for that ID then returns the stale local index instead of -1, so 'Bond/Angle atom missing' is not detected and neigh_bond builds a bond to an unrelated atom -> silently wrong forces instead of a hard error.
suggested_fix: Either drop the atom_map_legacy guard around map_clear() in exchange_device()/CommTiledKokkos, or add a device-side clear of k_map_array (deep_copy(view_device(),-1)) at the start of AtomKokkos::map_set_device() the way the hash branch already clears d_map_hash.

summary: k_exchange_copylist_bonus is marked modified on the host and synced to the device on every dimension of every exchange, even when there is no bonus data (bonus_flag == 0).
failure_scenario: Any non-bonus atom style: three needless host->device copies of k_exchange_copylist_bonus per exchange() call (once per dimension), plus a modify/sync flag toggle on a view nothing reads.
suggested_fix: Move the modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>() pair inside the 'if (bonus_flag)' block.

summary: grow_send_kokkos() sizes the send buffer with the constant Comm::BUFEXTRA instead of the Comm::bufextra member, so the extra headroom the legacy CommBrick::exchange() relies on (maxexchange + BUFEXTRA) is not provided.
failure_scenario: Legacy exchange path (package kokkos comm no, or gpu/aware off with >1 rank) with a style whose per-atom exchange size is large (many bonds/angles per atom, or fixes contributing a large maxexchange_fix): AtomVec::pack_exchange writes past the end of k_buf_send's host allocation.
suggested_fix: Use the Comm::bufextra member (kept up to date by Comm::init_exchange()) instead of Comm::BUFEXTRA, and round the row count up rather than down when dividing by size_border.

summary: CommTiledKokkos::forward_comm_device(): in the generic (non comm_x_only, non ghost_velocity) branch the self-send case packs the buffer but never unpacks it, so the ghost atoms this rank sends to itself never receive their forward-communicated data.
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled with the KOKKOS device forward comm (package kokkos comm device, the GPU default) and either (a) an atom style whose forward comm is not x-only -- atom_style dipole (mu), spin (sp), dpd/react (dpdTheta,uCond,uMech,uChem) -- or (b) any atom style in a single/mixed-precision KOKKOS build, where atomKK->k_x.NEED_TRANSFORM is true and even plain x takes this branch.  Whenever a rank is its own neighbour for a swap (sendself[iswap] != 0, normal with periodic boundaries and few tiles), the self ghosts keep the values from the last borders() call for the whole reneighbouring interval -> wrong forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->avecKK->unpack_comm_kokkos(recvnum[iswap][nrecv],firstrecv[iswap][nrecv],k_buf_send);' after the pack_comm_kokkos call in the sendself block, matching the ghost_velocity branch and CommTiled::forward_comm().

summary: DomainKokkos::pbc() drops the base class check that owned-atom coordinates are finite, so a blown-up KOKKOS run silently continues with NaN/Inf positions instead of aborting with the documented error.
failure_scenario: A KOKKOS GPU run whose pair style produces an infinite force (two atoms at the same position, bad initial configuration).  On the CPU (or with 'package kokkos comm no') LAMMPS stops with 'Non-numeric atom coords - simulation unstable'; on the device path the NaNs propagate silently and the run ends with garbage output or a much later, unrelated failure.
suggested_fix: Add a Kokkos::parallel_reduce over nlocal that ORs !isfinite(x(i,d)) into a flag (it can be folded into the existing PBC functor as a reduction) and call error->one() with the same message when the flag is set.

summary: DomainKokkos declares 'int closest_image(const int, int) const;' which is never defined anywhere and hides the three Domain::closest_image() overloads for anyone holding a DomainKokkos*.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.h:50: 'int closest_image(const int, int) const;'.  'grep -rn "DomainKokkos::closest_image" src' finds no definition; src/domain.h:143-145 declares the three non-virtual base overloads 'int closest_image(int, int); int closest_image(const double *const, int); void closest_image(const double *const, const double *const, double *const);' which name lookup in DomainKokkos would hide.  The KOKKOS callers (fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp:1031, fix_shake_kokkos.cpp:2388, neigh_bond_kokkos.cpp) each define their own closest_image member instead.
failure_scenario: Any new code that calls domain->closest_image(...) through a DomainKokkos pointer gets either an undefined-symbol link error (two-int form) or a compile error (the other overloads are hidden).
suggested_fix: Delete the declaration, or implement it and mark it as an explicit using-declaration of the base overloads.

summary: DynamicalMatrixKokkos::setup() is never called: the base DynamicalMatrix::setup() is not virtual and DynamicalMatrix::command() calls it non-virtually, so the KOKKOS setup (auto_sync bracketing plus the synced pair->compute) is dead code.
evidence: src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h:23 declares 'void setup();' with no 'virtual'.  src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.h:35 declares 'void setup();' with no 'override' (it cannot have one).  src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.cpp, DynamicalMatrix::command(): 'if (style == REGULAR) { setup(); ...' -- an unqualified call inside a DynamicalMatrix member, statically bound to DynamicalMatrix::setup().  The KOKKOS version (src/KOKKOS/dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:91-134) sets 'lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;' for the duration of the domain/comm/neighbor setup, adds an atomKK->sync()/modified() wrapped force->pair->compute(), and clears auto_sync to 0 at the end -- none of which runs.  This is the exact shape of rule 2 in .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md ('Declare virtual void allocate() in the base-class header ... without virtual, the base version is silently called').  src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.cpp:91 has the identical dead override against src/PHONON/third_order.h:23.
failure_scenario: 'dynamical_matrix/kk all regular 0.000001' on a GPU build: the base setup() runs, so lmp->kokkos->auto_sync is left at its default 1 for the whole calculateMatrix() loop and every atomKK->modified() call forces a full host<->device copy of the per-atom arrays -- the KOKKOS command runs at roughly host speed.  Any future correctness fix put into the KOKKOS setup() would also be silently ignored.
suggested_fix: Make DynamicalMatrix::setup() (and ThirdOrder::setup()) virtual in src/PHONON/dynamical_matrix.h / third_order.h and mark the KOKKOS versions 'override'.

summary: update_force() allocates a fresh f_merge_copy device view on every force evaluation, although the code further down already grows it on demand.
failure_scenario: dynamical_matrix does 6*N force evaluations; each one performs (and frees) a 3*nmax device allocation, which serialises against the device stream and dominates the runtime for large systems on a GPU.
suggested_fix: Drop the line 152 allocation and rely on the size check at lines 282-285 (same as VerletKokkos does).

summary: norm_functor stores the FFT normalization factor in an 'int' member, so the 1/(nfast*nmid*nslow) scaling is truncated to 0 and a scaled backward FFT would zero the whole output array.
failure_scenario: Any FFT3dKokkos created with scaled=1 (the constructor argument) returns an all-zero backward transform.  Currently latent because the only in-tree caller, src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:879-887, passes scaled=0 and does its own scaling; a new KOKKOS kspace style (or a fix to PPPM) that requests scaling silently gets zeros instead of an error.
suggested_fix: Change the functor member and constructor parameter to FFT_SCALAR (matching plan->norm / src/KSPACE/fft3d.cpp).

summary: The KISS FFT path allocates a fresh 'fft_3d:tmp' device view for each of the three 1d FFT stages on every fft_3d_kokkos() call instead of keeping a scratch view in the plan.
failure_scenario: KISS FFT is the default when no vendor FFT library is enabled; pppm/kk performs 4 FFTs per timestep, so this is 12 device allocate/free pairs per timestep, each of which serialises the device stream.
suggested_fix: Add a persistent tmp view to fft_plan_3d_kokkos (allocated once in fft_3d_create_plan_kokkos, sized like d_scratch) and reuse it in all three stages.

summary: The KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA (and SYCL) FFT-library fallback blocks forget to undefine FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL, unlike the HIP block, so a CUDA+NVPL build ends up with both NVPL and KISS defined and fails to compile instead of falling back to KISS.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fftdata_kokkos.h:43-55 (CUDA) undefines FFT_KOKKOS_FFTW, FFT_KOKKOS_FFTW3 and FFT_KOKKOS_MKL and then '#if !defined(FFT_KOKKOS_CUFFT) && !defined(FFT_KOKKOS_KISS) / #define FFT_KOKKOS_KISS'; the HIP block at lines 56-71 additionally does '# if defined(FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL)\n#  undef FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL\n# endif'.  The SYCL block (lines 72-84) also omits it.  With CUDA + -DFFT_KOKKOS_NVPL both FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL and FFT_KOKKOS_KISS are then defined: the typedef chain at lines 145-153 picks the fftw_complex FFT_KOKKOS_DATA, while line 268 still includes kissfft_kokkos.h, whose kernels use the '.re'/'.im' members of the KISS struct.
failure_scenario: 'make' with the traditional build (or any non-CMake configuration) using the Kokkos CUDA backend and -DFFT_KOKKOS_NVPL: a confusing compile error inside kissfft_kokkos.h instead of the intended silent fallback to KISS.  CMake blocks this combination (cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:224-226 FATAL_ERROR), which is why it has not been seen.
suggested_fix: Add the '#if defined(FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL) / #undef FFT_KOKKOS_NVPL / #endif' stanza to the CUDA and SYCL blocks, matching the HIP block.

summary: Grid3dKokkos::forward_comm()/reverse_comm() select the brick vs tiled path from the live comm->layout, while the matching data structures were built from the snapshot Grid3d::layout_grid taken at construction, so a layout change during a run makes the two disagree.
failure_scenario: Any sequence where comm->layout flips to LAYOUT_TILED after this Grid3dKokkos was set up but before it is destroyed (e.g. a balance/rcb between the grid setup and the next kspace comm): forward_comm() then takes the tiled branch while nsend/nrecv/ncopy are all still 0 from setup_comm_brick(), so no ghost grid data is exchanged at all and PPPM silently uses stale/zero ghost planes.  Currently masked because fix balance calls kspace->reset_grid() immediately after changing comm->layout.
suggested_fix: Use the inherited layout_grid member in both dispatchers (and fix the misleading indentation of the if/else while there).

summary: GroupKokkos::angmom_kk() uses the raw atom velocity instead of the deformation-corrected velocity, so with 'fix deform ... remap v' the angular momentum differs from Group::angmom() by the h_rate image term.
failure_scenario: 'fix deform ... remap v' together with 'fix momentum N group angular' (src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:135 calls angmom_kk) or 'fix addtorque/group' (src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_group_kokkos.cpp:98): for any atom of the deform group with a nonzero image flag the velocity used is the peculiar velocity instead of the streaming-corrected one, so the removed/applied angular momentum is wrong and the /kk run silently disagrees with the same input run without -k on.
suggested_fix: Add a DomainKokkos::unmap overload that also returns the corrected velocity (taking h_rate, deform_vremap and deform_groupbit as captured scalars) and use it in angmom_kk, matching Domain::unmap(x,v,image,mask,y,u).

summary: vcm_kk() forms the momentum products in KK_FLOAT (float in single/mixed precision) before widening to the double accumulator, unlike every other reduction in the same file and unlike Group::vcm().
failure_scenario: A mixed-precision KOKKOS build (KOKKOS_PRECISION=mixed) running 'fix momentum linear' or 'compute temp/com' (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_com_kokkos.cpp:57): each term of the center-of-mass velocity is rounded to float before summation, so the removed drift and the temperature bias carry single-precision error even though the accumulator is double.
suggested_fix: Cast d_v(i,*) and massone to double before multiplying, as the other kernels in this header do.

summary: PPPMKokkos shadows PPPM::gc and never overrides PPPM::reset_grid(), so a load-balance rebalance runs the CPU reset_grid on the KOKKOS style: it calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff(), which writes the base rho_coeff array that a KOKKOS run never allocates (nullptr), and dereferences the base gc, which is also nullptr.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:103-108:
  // same name but different than base class
  gc = nullptr; fft1 = nullptr; fft2 = nullptr; remap = nullptr;
(these assign the PPPMKokkos members declared in src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:449, which shadow PPPM::gc etc.; PPPM's own gc is set to nullptr at src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:80 and never re-assigned in a KOKKOS run).  'grep -rn reset_grid src/KOKKOS' finds nothing, so PPPM::reset_grid (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668) is inherited unchanged; it runs
  allocate();                                   // virtual -> PPPMKokkos::allocate, which creates only k_rho_coeff (pppm_kokkos.cpp:865) and never memory->create2d_offset(rho_coeff,...) as PPPM::allocate does at pppm.cpp:913
  if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) // base gc == nullptr
  compute_rho_coeff();                          // NOT virtual (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142) -> PPPM::compute_rho_coeff writes 'rho_coeff[l][m] = a[l][k];' (pppm.cpp:2930) with rho_coeff == nullptr
reset_grid() is called on every rebalance: src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'.
failure_scenario: 'fix balance ... rcb' (or shift) in a run with kspace_style pppm/kk: the rebalance calls kspace->reset_grid(), which segfaults in PPPM::compute_rho_coeff (null rho_coeff); with 'kspace_modify overlap no' it segfaults one line earlier on the null base gc.  Even if the pointers were valid, the KOKKOS device copies (k_rho_coeff / d_rho_coeff, re-created uninitialized by PPPMKokkos::allocate) would never be filled or synced, since PPPMKokkos::init() is the only place that does compute_rho_coeff() + k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync (pppm_kokkos.cpp:277-281).
suggested_fix: Give PPPMKokkos an override of reset_grid() that mirrors PPPM::reset_grid but uses the KOKKOS gc and calls PPPMKokkos::compute_rho_coeff() followed by k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>(); alternatively make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff virtual and stop shadowing gc.  NOTE: pppm_kokkos.cpp is outside this reviewer's assigned file list (found while tracing Grid3dKokkos callers).
